title: Cosmic-ray-boosted and otherwise fast light dark matter at the extended LZ window: can a relativistic light particle leave a lone 248 keV recoil?
question: Can sub-GeV DM boosted to beta ~ 0.1-1 (CRDM, blazar/decay-boosted) or a fast TeV sub-population produce a 248 keV Xe recoil without a 5.4-55 keV population; what N_lo results for beams, power-law and CRDM spectra with Helm and shell-model form factors; what sigma_chi p gives one LZ event and is it excluded by CRDM searches or Earth attenuation?
headline_result: For any velocity-independent contact interaction a relativistic beam gives N_lo >= 350 (Helm) / 1184 (shell) low-energy events per 200-270 keV event, a floor set by the nuclear response (F2(30)/F2(248) = 1249/6809) and independent of incident spectrum, mass or speed; CRDM needs sigma_chi p = 3.6-6.3e-30 cm^2 (m <= 100 MeV), inside recalled XENON1T/PandaX-4T exclusions, and predicts 2e3-6e4 events in LZ's 5.4-55 keV ROI; at m >= 1 GeV the required sigma exceeds the Earth-attenuation ceiling; a fast TeV SI component has the same N_lo = 350/1184; only q^4-spin couplings (N_lo 0.18) pass
key_numbers: T_min(248) 122/114/59/7.7/0.89 MeV (1/10/100 MeV/1/10 GeV), p_min 123 MeV/c, neutron 8.17 MeV; N_lo flat 349.9 Helm/1184 shell (P030: 353/1182), q2 33/114, q4 4.1/14, q4 Sigma'' 0.18, SHM 1 TeV Helm 820; vector endpoint-tuned beam 757/2528; CRDM-spectrum N_lo 1.7e4/1.5e4/2.2e3/762/675 (Helm); Phi(T>Tmin) at 1e-30, 1 kpc: 2.1e-7/1.3e-7/5.2e-8/2.4e-9/8.4e-11; sigma_p(1 event) 3.6/4.4/6.3e-30, 2.4e-29 (1-10 GeV), x1.85 shell, x0.32 at 10 kpc; attenuation 30% ceiling 3.8/3.3/1.2e-28, 4.0e-30 (1 GeV), 1.9e-32 (10 GeV); TeV beta 0.005-0.02 E_R,max 4.9-92 MeV
model_or_mechanism: exact relativistic two-body kinematics; flat-in-E_R beam spectra with constant, vector-, scalar- and pseudoscalar-mediator amplitude structures folded with Helm (lzcommon) and shell-model (P017/WimPyDD) M and Sigma'' responses and P003 efficiency; Bringmann-Pospelov CRDM flux from the PDG proton spectrum with proton dipole FF; coherent A^2 rate in 4.71 t x 220 d; mean-energy-loss attenuation in standard rock
stance: neutral (tool, projection, or constraint) - excludes boosted SI light DM and fast SI components
result_type: computed (kinematics, N_lo floor, attenuation) / estimated (CRDM normalisation, recalled limits)
confidence: high for the N_lo floor (response-only, reproduces P030); medium for CRDM normalisation and recalled exclusion bands
